newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-DORTMUND COACH HINTS AT LEADERSHIP PROBLEMS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DORTMUND COACH HINTS AT LEADERSHIP PROBLEMS.

text.p: Ottmar Hitzfeld, coach of European Cup winners Borussia Dortmund, hinted on Wednesday at management problems at the club whose long-serving president announced earlier this week he was quitting.

Gerd Niebaum, whose 11-year presidency of the club was among the most successful in Dortmund's history, said on Tuesday he was stepping down to spend more time with his family and concentrate on his career in charge of a large law firm.
But Hitzfeld, in an interview with the newspaper Die Zeit, said he had been disappointed by Niebaum's failure to back efforts to resolve long-standing morale problems at the club.
"Of course I thought Gerd Niebaum could have helped correct the negative mood when it first started," Hitzfeld said.

Hitzfeld prompted questions over his own future after last week's 3-1 victory against Italy's Juventus by telling reporters that continued criticism within the club about the weak second half of its season had "given him cause to think".
He acknowledged that relations between him and his team were not perfect. "The relationship is good -- or let's just say 'normal'," he said.
While stepping down had crossed his mind, he was not seriously considering it as an option, he said.
"I'm not the sort of guy who throws in the towel. It is possible to discuss difficulties with each other," he said.
